person.label: Person
person.says: An author, editor, translator — or an institution that issued a document.

name.label: Name
name.says: The full name when it does not split into given names and surname (e.g. "Francis", "St Augustine", "Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith")

givenNames.label: Given names
givenNames.says: Given names — shortened to initials in footnotes

surname.label: Surname
surname.says: Surname — the bibliography is sorted by it

description.label: Description
description.says: A short description of the person (biography) — shown with their sources

url.label: Website
url.says: A page about this person (e.g. a biography)

more.choir: performer — a choir as an institution

id.label: Identifier
id.says: A fixed identifier of the file in the list; omitted — assigned automatically

label.label: What it is
label.hint: e.g. Full score · Soprano · Organ · MusicXML

file.label: File
file.says: A file uploaded in the app (PDF, image, MusicXML, MIDI)

id.label: Identifier
id.says: A fixed identifier of the track; omitted — assigned automatically

label.label: Voice / instrument
label.says: Whose voice or which instrument — or “Whole”
label.hint: e.g. Soprano · Alto · Tenor · Bass · Organ · Whole

role.label: Role
role.says: "part" — a voice or instrument: played together with the other tracks of this recording; "whole" — the whole recording: played on its own

file.label: File
file.says: An audio file uploaded in the app (MP3, OGG, M4A, WAV, FLAC)

work.label: Source
work.says: A work you use: a book, chapter, article, Church document, Holy Scripture, website — or music: a piece, sheet music, a recording, an album.

workType.label: Type
workType.says: Type: {types}; music: {music}. The type decides which fields the work has

title.label: Title
title.says: Title of the work (piece, recording, album)

subtitle.label: Subtitle
subtitle.says: Subtitle (or the kind of document, e.g. "apostolic exhortation")

originalTitle.label: Original title
originalTitle.says: Original title (the original title of a translation; for a piece — the title in the original language)

otherTitles.label: Other titles, incipit
otherTitles.says: Other names people know the piece by — incipit (first words), a title in another language, a common name; one per line
otherTitles.hint: e.g. Lord, you have come to the lakeshore

authors.label: Authors
authors.says: Authors — references to people, in order (for music: composer, lyricist — fields below)

composers.label: Composer
composers.says: Composers — references to people; sheet music and recordings that point to the piece need not repeat them

lyricists.label: Lyricist
lyricists.says: Lyricists of the piece — references to people

arrangers.label: Arrangement
arrangers.says: Who arranged (harmonised, arranged) the piece in this version — references to people

translators.label: Translation
translators.says: Translators — references to people (for a piece: translation of the lyrics)

performers.label: Performers
performers.says: Who performs — choir, ensemble, conductor, soloists: references to people and institutions

piece.label: Piece
piece.says: Which piece this sheet music notates or this recording performs — a reference to a work with "workType": "piece"

album.label: On album
album.says: The album this recording is on — a reference to a work with "workType": "album"

track.label: Track no.
track.says: Number of the recording on the album

container.label: In (book, periodical)
container.says: For a chapter: the book; for an article: the periodical — a reference to a source

volume.label: Volume / year
volume.says: Volume (book, collection of sheet music) or annual volume (periodical)

catalogue.label: Catalogue number
catalogue.says: For a piece: the number in the catalogue of works (op. 27 no. 2, BWV 147, KV 618); for sheet music and albums: the publisher's number

voicing.label: Scoring
voicing.hint: e.g. SATB a cappella · mixed choir and organ · unison

genre.label: Genre
genre.says: What kind of piece or book it is (novel, biographical novel, biography, reportage, missal, prayer book, textbook…)
genre.hint: e.g. hymn, psalm, motet · biographical novel, missal

publisher.label: Publisher
publisher.says: Publishing house (for recordings and albums: the label)

year.label: Year
year.says: Year of publication (or the date of a document; for a piece — the year it was written, for a recording — the year it was recorded)

series.label: Series
series.says: Publisher's series, with the volume number in the series

pages.label: Pages
pages.says: Page range of the chapter or article

pageCount.label: Number of pages
pageCount.says: How many pages the book has

length.label: Thickness (cm)
length.says: The third dimension — thickness (depth of the spine) in centimetres

siglum.label: Translation abbreviation
siglum.says: For Holy Scripture: the abbreviation of the translation, added to the sigla

isbn.label: ISBN
isbn.says: The book's ISBN (with or without hyphens; several — separated by commas)

ismn.label: ISMN
ismn.says: ISMN of the sheet music edition

libraryNumber.label: Library number
libraryNumber.says: This library's own number for the copy (inventory number, shelf mark) — you can search for it and scan it

language.label: Language
language.says: Language (e.g. "pl", "la"; for music — the language of the lyrics)

lyrics.label: Lyrics
lyrics.says: Lyrics of the piece — verses separated by an empty line

scheme.label: Place layout
scheme.says: How places in this work are referred to: {list}; empty — from the type (Holy Scripture: bible, document: numbered, recording: time — minutes and seconds, others: pages)

pageSeries.label: Page series
pageSeries.says: When a book numbers its parts separately (introduction, appendices, inserts): one sample page from each series, as printed, in the book's order, separated by spaces — e.g. "xii 12* 1 3' (1) A1" (roman, with an asterisk, plain, with an apostrophe, in brackets, with a letter; any marks are possible). Page "12*" and page "12" are two different pages. Empty — roman, then plain, then the rest

psalms.label: Psalm numbering
psalms.says: For Holy Scripture: "hebrew" (Hebrew — most modern translations) or "greek" (Greek — Septuagint, Vulgate)

editionOf.label: Edition / translation of the work
editionOf.says: This is another edition or translation of that work — a reference to a source. Places in the structure (verse, number, paragraph) are shared by all editions; pages are not.

files.label: Sheet music files
files.says: Files of this sheet music — full score, parts, notation; files are uploaded in the app, JSON from an export carries them within the same library

tracks.label: Tracks
tracks.says: Files of the recording — the whole recording or separate voices and instruments played together; files are uploaded in the app, JSON from an export carries them within the same library

quote.label: Quote
quote.says: A passage from a source — with its place (page, verse, number) and a description.

text.label: Quote text
text.says: The exact wording of the quote

translation.label: Translation
translation.says: Translation of the quote (when the text is in another language)

id.label: Identifier
id.says: A fixed identifier of the point (e.g. "p4k2x"); omitted — assigned automatically. Deliveries refer to points by it

text.label: Content
text.says: The thought in one or two sentences, in content markup: [@key, s. 12] — a source, ![@quote-key] alone — a quote from the library

depth.label: Level
depth.says: 0 — main thought, 1 — under it, 2 — deeper still

point.label: Plan point
point.says: "id" of the point in the text's plan

at.label: Time
at.says: When this point starts in the recording (mm:ss or hh:mm:ss)

note.label: Note
note.says: What was different from the plan

area.label: Class
area.says: Identifier of the class's area (from an export or from the school's card)

text.label: What
text.says: What was said (one or two sentences), in content markup

after.label: After point
after.says: "id" of the plan point after which it was said; empty — at the end

text.label: Text
text.says: Your own text — a sermon, a meditation, a book chapter — with references to sources and quotes.

textType.label: Text type
textType.says: Your own text type — a reference (e.g. "@kazanie-maryjne"); its extra fields then stand next to the text's fields. Omitted — a plain text

project.label: Project (book, series)
project.says: Which book or series it belongs to — a reference

date.label: Date delivered / written
date.says: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) — the archive is ordered by it

summary.label: Short description
summary.says: Short description — in the archive, above the content

plan.label: Plan
plan.says: Plan — the main thoughts in order, under them quotes, examples, questions, applications; a list of points { "id", "text", "depth", "kind", "note" }. Deliveries refer to points by "id"

body.label: Content
body.says: Content in simple markup (below: "Content markup") — with references [@key, s. 12]

further.label: Further information
further.says: Further information below the text — in the same markup

targetWords.label: Target word count
targetWords.says: How many words it should have

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.says: One delivery of a prepared text (sermon, talk): when and where, the recording — and what of the plan was said, what only briefly, what was skipped and what was added.

texts.label: Sermon (text)
texts.says: Which prepared text was delivered — a reference (usually one; several when material was combined)

date.label: Date
date.says: When (YYYY-MM-DD) — the archive is ordered by it

readings.label: Readings
readings.says: Readings of the day, biblical sigla

audio.label: Recording (address)
audio.says: Address of the audio recording — a file (mp3, m4a, ogg) or a page with the recording

video.label: Video (address)
video.says: Address of the video recording — a file (mp4, webm) or YouTube

summary.label: About this delivery
summary.says: What mattered most this time, how it differed

coverage.label: What of the plan
coverage.says: What of the text's plan was said — point by point: { "point", "state", "at", "note" }

added.label: What was added
added.says: What was said but was not in the plan: { "text", "at", "after" }

transcript.label: Transcript
transcript.says: What was said, written down word for word — in content markup

classArea.label: Class
classArea.says: A lesson at school: identifier of the area of the class in which this lesson took (or is to take) place; omitted — an ordinary delivery

state.label: Lesson state
state.says: Only a lesson in a class: {list}; omitted — held

homework.label: Task for the class
homework.says: Only a lesson in a class: homework or what the class should prepare

project.label: Project
project.says: A book, sermon series, collection — with a plan (chapters, parts) and writing progress.

description.label: Description
description.says: Description of the project — what the book or series is about

outline.label: Plan
outline.says: Plan: a list of {"heading": "Part I"} and {"text": reference to a text} in order; a reader sees the texts they may read

targetWords.label: Target word count
targetWords.says: How many words the whole should have

classes.label: Classes
classes.says: A school curriculum: the classes that follow it — a list { "area": identifier of the class's area }

textType.label: Text type
textType.says: Your own text type (e.g. “Marian sermon”): a name and extra fields that every text of this type has — including references to entries in Knowledge (e.g. mystery, area). A text without a type is a plain text.

name.label: Name
name.says: Name of the type, e.g. “Marian sermon”

fields.label: Extra fields
fields.says: Fields every text of this type has — described like the fields of a kind in Knowledge: a list {"key", "label", "type", "multi", "options", "to", "locator", "says"}. "type": line, text, number, date, bool, choice, ref, url, list. For "ref" — "to": names of kinds in Knowledge (e.g. ["Tajemnica"]) or "work", "quote", "person" from the library; "locator": true — with a place (e.g. Holy Scripture + "Łk 1,26-38"). The keys of the text's fixed fields (title, date, plan, body …) are taken

musicSays.piece: the piece itself: composer, lyrics, key, scoring
musicSays.score: an edition of sheet music, with files: full score, parts, notation
musicSays.recording: a performance: one file or several tracks (voices and instruments, played together)
